observed_behavior: A valid owner and worker could not service queue commands when a retained sibling directory lost its native Git metadata.
expected_behavior: Queue commands validate the invoking checkout and its owner without requiring unrelated retained checkouts to remain healthy.
causal_mechanism: The CLI used full swarm inventory as its owner resolver; inventory checked Git metadata in every recorded sibling and propagated a sibling not-a-repository error before executing a queue command.

anti_pattern.structural_description: An operational request depends on a broader inventory health sweep than its authority and resource scope.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Failure of an unrelated retained checkout stops a valid coordinator from servicing help and recovery requests.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Resolve one exact project/root owner and validate the actual actor and repository at execution.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Query owner/membership for the invoking root only, reject ambiguity, and retain strict SwarmQueueStore actor validation. Full inventory remains a separate inspection.

applicability_conditions: A project has multiple managed roots and one existing sibling loses Git metadata.
known_non_matches: Invalid invoking owner or worker identities remain rejected by the execution boundary.
confirmation_evidence: Disposable sibling with removed .git reproduced the same fatal not-a-repository failure through the real queue CLI.
regression_proofs: tests/swarm-queue.integration.test.ts: autonomous queues preserve parked work, race exclusive claims, service FIFO and publish discovery through real CLI; worker status and coordinator take pass with stale retained sibling
